title: King Oliver's trumpet advice: playing the upper register on the lip
summary: Oliver taught Phillips to play the high notes by lipping with less valve work, as Louis had after playing bugle as a boy.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: How about the things that he told you about the horn itself? What things did you maybe learn from seeing him?
Well, he told me about the horn like this. He told me, he said, 'When you're up in the upper register, you can make all those notes without dropping...'

After you get up in the upper register, he said you can make C, D, E, F --- he said 'You can play the whole scale up there on the lip, without the fingering.' He said that when you get down in the register, you've got to make A-sharp, you make that with one valve basically, going back over and hitting the two-valve to make it. He said, 'While you're there, stay there. Don't move. If you've got a fast passage, when you get ready to play something, you just play it on...'

He said a lot of things Louis did... He said Louis was the best lipper ever blew a horn. You know what I mean? He could blow them... He could blow them notes, and didn't have to do a whole lot of fingering. Because, see, Louis played a bugle when he was a kid, delivering coal. And he got so he could play that bugle like he played the trumpet. You know, the bugle ain't got no keys on it. He was lippin'. So he said, 'That's the way it is. Then you play those notes like that, then you get in the habit of doing it. Then when you get to the fast passages, you don't have to go way back there on the second and third valves. You could just make it with
the first valve. You don't have to go back there. A lot of things like that he showed me.
